My forecast is that it's going to be *very* dependent on who reads it. Some are going to panic at the very sight of "Rubik", others are going to recognize it for the trivial problem it is.

The more general point is: it's the easiest in the series, but it has its place. It's doable in clash (hence my submitting it there), but it could actually make sense to duplicate it to community puzzles once the others "can it be solved this way" are approved, to enable a more gradual difficulty slope.

My proposed sample solution is 78 characters (though I'll admit I didn't spend as much on it as I would have on a clash). How long is yours? :D
i've taken the liberty to fix the missing space in last test case

Thanks for the report, thanks for solving.
I think it's fine in reverse; moreover it's been there long enough that if clashers thought it weren't, it would have been autoremoved from this mode by now.

To elaborate on the reverse mode: this is subjective, but in my opinion (1) it might not be clear that this is a rubik's cube, (2) there is pretty much no way to figure out that the cube is being solved using the "Restickering™ method" in reverse mode. Moreover, I don't think anyone will assume that it is the case without having access to the statement. So most reverse solutions likely just assume that only a smaller subset of checks is required for this specific problem, like checking the number of stickers, maybe checking the central faces have unique stickers, maybe checking that all the unique pieces of a rubik's cube are in place (like 8 correct corner pieces, 12 edge ones and again 6 face ones), etc. That is, there are a lot of checks one might want to / assume they need to implement. The only cases where Restickering solves the cube but the cube itself is unsolvable using normal methods are (I assume) ones with an edge flip or a corner twist, but they are quite a bit further down in the available tests and are hardly noticeable, and even if one notices it, there is no indication that "solvability" is determined by the Restickering; instead one might assume we just allow edge flips / corner twists --- and that is even if we assume one knows what edge flips / corner twists are (and I wouldn't assume those to be common knowledge)

P.S. thanks for answering :)
